question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Seismic precursor monitoring: live-cell reporter time series before drug addition
ideas.description: Seismologists look for small signals that come before an earthquake. In the same spirit, image thousands of cells for 48–72 h before treatment using fluorescent reporters for key pathways (e.g., ERK/AKT KTR sensors, a NF-κB or AP-1 reporter), then add the drug and track which cells survive. Train a classifier on the pre-drug traces to test whether survivors show dynamic signatures beforehand, such as pulsing frequency or variance, rather than just steady-state levels.

ideas.title: Ecological bet-hedging assay: fluctuation analysis of the primed state
ideas.description: Plants spread germination across seasons as a hedge against bad years. Borrowing that idea, run a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test: expand many single-cell-derived clones for different numbers of generations, treat them in parallel, and fit survivor-count distributions. This estimates how often cells switch into and out of the drug-tolerant state and how long that state is inherited, which separates stochastic hedging from fixed heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Materials fatigue testing: graded drug-pulse stress protocols
ideas.description: Engineers learn how materials fail by applying cyclic, graded loads instead of a single break test. Expose cells to systematically varied drug pulse lengths, doses and recovery intervals, then measure survivor fractions alongside single-cell RNA-seq at each step. Mapping the dose-history response surface shows whether survival comes from a pre-existing state, adaptation the drug induces, or both, and where the transition happens.

ideas.title: Epidemiological contact tracing: spatial neighbor analysis of survivors
ideas.description: Contact tracing in epidemiology finds out whether cases cluster because of shared exposures. Use high-plex spatial imaging (e.g., multiplexed smFISH or CODEX) on treated cultures and organoids to check whether survivors are enriched near particular neighbors, local densities, or secreted-factor gradients. Then test the candidate niche signals with conditioned-media and co-culture perturbations.

ideas.title: Network percolation: CRISPR perturbation of the transition between states
ideas.description: Percolation theory looks at how removing individual nodes changes whether a whole network stays connected. Run pooled CRISPRi/a screens with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) to find regulators whose knockdown or activation shifts how often cells reach the tolerant state. Fitting a gene-regulatory network model to these results then identifies the hub factors whose shared fluctuations push a cell over the survival threshold.
